page: Microsoft Azure D32pls_v6 is a virtualized server within the Dplsv6 series, configured with 32 dedicated arm64 cores based on the ARM Neoverse-N2 microarchitecture running at 3.4 GHz. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V with one hardware thread per physical core, the configuration includes 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 128 MB L3 cache pool. The instance is provisioned with 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation. It includes no bundled local storage and features zero GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage for persistent disk access.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant multi-threaded throughput and memory bus capability. The instance achieves top-tier results in uncached memory bandwidth, reaching 449.06 GB/sec for large reads and 188.51 GB/sec for writes, alongside top-tier database operations testing. Multi-core performance is strong in stress-ng evaluations at 66293.46 and Clang software compilation at 40457.0. Single-core performance across Geekbench and stress-ng falls within average tiers. Text generation and prompt processing for large 70B parameter language models show lower throughput due to memory capacity and core architecture constraints.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio represents an efficiency-oriented compute density tradeoff, providing substantial core count without the overhead of oversized memory allocations. Strong multi-threaded decompression and static web serving throughput reaching 50.4 GB/sec align this server with parallel, scale-out services. The D32pls_v6 is appropriate for continuous integration build farms, containerized microservices, static web infrastructure, and multi-threaded data transformation jobs.
description: Microsoft Azure D32pls_v6 is an ARM-based compute instance powered by 32 dedicated Neoverse-N2 cores running at 3.4 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. It features 64 GB of memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core allocation, alongside 128 MB of L3 cache. The system has zero GPUs and no bundled local storage, operating with remote storage attachments. Benchmark metrics show top-tier memory bandwidth exceeding 449 GB/sec read and 188 GB/sec write on large blocks, paired with strong multi-core performance in Clang compilation and multi-threaded stress testing. While single-thread benchmarks and large language model inference place in mid-to-lower tiers, the platform demonstrates high multi-core efficiency. The D32pls_v6 is well aligned with compute-focused workloads including software compilation, web serving, microservices hosting, and parallel data processing pipelines.
